subject: MSA + Order Form: physical injury/property damage cap — counterproposal
summary: Customer requested a carve-out from the MSA liability cap for personal injury and property damage. Sales looped legal; legal proposes a limited sub-cap and narrow scope as compromise. Customer conditionally accepts; final confirmation pending third-party hardware scope.
messages:
From: Jessica Sullivan <jessica.sullivan@acmeinc.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeinc.com
Date: Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: RE: MSA/redlines attached — liability carve-out request

Jonas — attaching Acme's redlines to the MSA and Order Form. Our procurement team cannot take any capped exposure for "personal injury or physical property damage" arising from use of the service (we have regulatory reporting obligations and campus safety policies).

Key ask: remove personal injury/property damage from the liability cap and any aggregate cap in the Order Form.

Can you confirm if Redwood will accept an unlimited carve-out for those categories? If not, what alternative does Redwood propose so we can move to signatures this week?

Attachments: Acme_Redlines_MSA_20270401.pdf (redline PDF)

Thanks,
Jessica Sullivan
Sr. Procurement Manager — Acme Inc.
procurement@acmeinc.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jessica Sullivan <jessica.sullivan@acmeinc.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 10:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: MSA/redlines attached — liability carve-out request

Jessica — thanks for the redlines and the clarity on Acme's procurement stance. I'm looping in Redwood legal (Ava) and our contracts lead (Karthik) to get a clean position.

High level: unlimited carve-outs are difficult for Redwood given enterprise exposure and reinsurance constraints. We want to get you to signature quickly — can you share whether this must be in the MSA or if an Order Form-level solution (sub-cap) would be acceptable? That flexibility might let us reach agreement faster.

Proposed next step: legal will propose language that narrows the scope and limit exposure while trying to address Acme's compliance concerns. Can you confirm your target signature date?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 08:45 AM PDT
Subject: Fwd: MSA/redlines attached — liability carve-out request (legal take)

Jonas/Karthik — my read after reviewing Acme's redlines: they seek to treat physical injury/property damage as an uncapped category. That is an outlier and creates open-ended exposure tied to events that are not plausibly caused by a SaaS runtime in most cases.

Suggested compromise (we can push in either direction depending on deal priority):
- Keep the MSA cap in place for all contractual damages but create a narrow exception for direct physical injury or physical property damage caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, with a sub-cap of USD 10,000,000 per incident and USD 20,000,000 aggregate across the term.
- Exclude consequential, lost profits, punitive damages as before; the carve-out only applies to direct third-party bodily injury or tangible property damage causally linked to Redwood's physical acts (e.g., on-prem hardware we installed or maintained) — not to data loss, model outputs, or downstream business interruption.
- Require notice, investigation cooperation, and mitigation steps prior to payout; drop hands-on remedies unless causation is established.

Rationale: a finite sub-cap addresses Acme's regulatory/compliance concern while controlling Redwood's actuarial exposure. If Acme refuses a sub-cap, we should consider escalating to sales leadership for sign-off on higher limits.

I've attached proposed language (RW-physical-damage-subcap-proposal.docx). Happy to redline further.

—Ava Chen
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jessica Sullivan <jessica.sullivan@acmeinc.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 11:20 AM PDT
Subject: RE: MSA/redlines attached — Redwood counterproposal on physical damage carve-out

Jessica — thank you and thanks for sharing the Acme team position. Redwood's legal team reviewed and we have a counterproposal that we think balances your compliance needs with Redwood's risk limits. Summary below and attached redline language.

What Redwood can accept (summary):
- A limited carve-out to the general liability cap that applies only to direct bodily injury and tangible property damage caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Sub-cap: USD 10,000,000 per incident, USD 20,000,000 aggregate for the Term.
- Carve-out excludes consequential, special, incidental, exemplary, and punitive damages.
- Carve-out applies only where causation to Redwood's physical act is shown (e.g., physical device or installation by Redwood). It does NOT apply to SaaS outputs, model predictions, or third-party cloud provider failures absent Redwood's gross negligence.
- Standard notice, cooperation, and mitigation prerequisites (30 days' notice, right to investigate, opportunity to remediate).

Why this should work: it gives Acme a finite recovery path for the categories you flagged while keeping Redwood's exposure capped and tied to direct, provable physical causation.

If Acme is comfortable with this approach, please confirm and we can incorporate the language into the MSA/Order Form and route for signature (DocuSign link below). If you need a different numeric cap for regulatory reasons, flag it and I will escalate.

DocuSign (proposal): https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/abc123
Attachments: RW-physical-damage-subcap-proposal.docx

Next steps: please let me know by EOD Monday Apr 5 if we should proceed on this basis, or if your legal team needs us to consider a higher sub-cap.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
From: Jessica Sullivan <jessica.sullivan@acmeinc.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeinc.com
Date: Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 01:37 PM PDT
Subject: Re: MSA/redlines attached — Redwood counterproposal on physical damage carve-out

Thanks Jonas — Acme legal and procurement reviewed the sub-cap approach and are willing to accept the proposed USD 10M / USD 20M framework in principle. One outstanding question from our counsel: does the carve-out include damage to Acme's physical property caused by third-party hardware that Acme owns but that interacts with Redwood's service (e.g., on-campus sensors that forward data to Redwood)? They want explicit language that clarifies "Redwood liability only where Redwood performed physical installation or maintenance leading to damage."

If that's your intent, please confirm and we will instruct our counsel to proceed to incorporate your redline and prepare the final Order Form for signature.

—Jessica
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Inc.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jessica Sullivan <jessica.sullivan@acmeinc.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 03:30 PM PDT
Subject: Re: MSA/redlines attached — Redwood counterproposal on physical damage carve-out

Jessica — confirmed. The carve-out is limited to direct physical harm or property damage where Redwood's physical act (installation, maintenance or similar hands-on service) is the proximate cause. Damage stemming from Acme-owned third-party hardware that merely transmits data to Redwood without Redwood's physical intervention would not fall into the carve-out.

We'll incorporate that clarifying sentence into the redline and re-share for final sign-off. If acceptable, I will route the revised MSA/Order Form to DocuSign and copy both legal teams.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
